items.title: U.S. Bank CFO Survey: Optimism Climbing as Growth and Dealmaking Gain Momentum
items.summary: A U.S. Bank CFO survey indicates growing optimism among corporate finance leaders regarding both the U.S. economy and their own businesses, with a notable shift in priorities towards revenue growth and M&A opportunities. While cost-cutting remains important, the focus is increasingly on strategic expansion and leveraging AI investments. Geopolitical risks, high borrowing costs, and inflation persist, but leaders are viewing uncertainty as an opportunity and addressing inflation through productivity improvements rather than layoffs.

items.title: I’m Jumping Back Into Taiwan Semiconductor Again and I Won’t Stop This Time
items.summary: The author is repeatedly investing in Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) due to its strong financials and critical role in AI chip manufacturing. TSM's 2nm ramp is significantly boosting revenue and margins, and its valuation is favorable compared to competitors like NVIDIA and Intel. The company has a clear roadmap through 2029, and despite risks like high capex and geopolitical concentration, the author remains confident in its long-term growth.

items.title: Target cuts prices on thousands of items ahead of holidays
items.summary: Target is reducing prices on nearly 2,000 items in anticipation of a value-driven holiday shopping season, building on over 10,000 price cuts from the past year. This move aims to appeal to inflation-weary consumers, particularly in apparel and home categories which have seen sluggish sales. The retailer is also planning a "Circle Deal Days" event to compete with Amazon's upcoming sales.

items.summary: Ford, JPMorgan Chase, and the state of Michigan are collaborating with Michigan Central Station and Newlab in Corktown to create a new $3 billion initiative. items.title: U.S. home prices rose 1.9% over the year, yet fell after inflation for a 14th straight month.
items.summary: The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index recorded a 1.9% annual gain in July 2026, an increase from 1.6% in June. However, after adjusting for inflation, U.S. home values declined for the 14th consecutive month, as consumer prices rose 3.4% annually. Regional disparities were significant, with Chicago showing the highest annual gain at 6.9% and Seattle experiencing the lowest return with a 1.6% fall.

items.title: Target Slashes Prices on Nearly 2,000 Products Ahead of Holiday Shopping Season
items.summary: Target Corporation is cutting prices on almost 2,000 products, including home goods, apparel, and accessories, to enhance its value proposition before the holiday shopping season. This move follows over 10,000 price reductions made in the past year and aligns with a broader retail trend, including Walmart's similar price cuts, to attract price-sensitive consumers amid inflation and higher gasoline costs. Target's strategy emphasizes affordability while maintaining style, as executives noted that value remains central to the company's approach given selective consumer spending.

items.title: Expand Energy Corp stock hits 52-week low at 84.42 USD
items.summary: Expand Energy Corp's stock has dropped to a 52-week low of 84.42 USD, marking a 19.7% decline over the past year. Despite this, the stock trades at a low P/E ratio of 7.37 and is considered undervalued by InvestingPro analysis, which also notes its oversold RSI and a perfect Piotroski Score. The company recently exceeded profit expectations but missed revenue targets in Q2, with differing analyst opinions on its future due to management changes, a weak natural gas market, and fluctuating oil prices.
